cuetRelevance.pyqFrequency: Core health domain topic. Tested frequently on disease vectors, communicable vs non-communicable categories, and government flagship schemes.

summary30Seconds: Communicable diseases spread via biological agents (air, water, vectors, contact): Malaria (Plasmodium via Anopheles), Tuberculosis (Mycobacterium tuberculosis), Cholera (Vibrio cholerae).
Non-communicable diseases (NCDs) are lifestyle and metabolic disorders: Diabetes Mellitus (insulin deficiency/resistance), Hypertension (>140/90 mmHg), Cardiovascular Diseases, Cancer.

National Health Programmes: National Tuberculosis Elimination Programme (NTEP - target elimination), National Vector Borne Disease Control Programme (NVBDCP), Ayushman Bharat (PM-JAY covering ₹5 lakh/family/year).
Community Hygiene: Safe drinking water, waste disposal (sanitary landfills/composting), sewage treatment, and vector control prevent epidemic outbreaks.

coreConcepts.title: 1. Communicable vs Non-Communicable Diseases (NCDs)
coreConcepts.content:
Communicable (Infectious) Diseases: Caused by pathogens (viruses, bacteria, fungi, protozoa) and transmitted from infected reservoir to susceptible host. Modes of transmission: Direct (physical contact, droplet spray like Influenza/COVID-19) and Indirect (water/food-borne like Typhoid/Cholera, vector-borne like Dengue by Aedes mosquito, fomite-borne). Prevention requires immunization, sanitation, quarantine, and chemotherapy.

Non-Communicable Diseases (NCDs): Chronic conditions that are not transmissible. Driven by lifestyle risk factors: tobacco use, physical inactivity, unhealthy diet, and alcohol abuse. Key NCDs: Cardiovascular Diseases (leading global cause of death; atherosclerosis and coronary artery disease), Diabetes (Type 1 autoimmune beta-cell destruction; Type 2 lifestyle insulin resistance), Chronic Respiratory Diseases (Asthma, COPD), and Cancer.
ncertPointers: Tuberculosis is detected via Mantoux tuberculin skin test and Sputum Microscopy; treated with DOTS (Directly Observed Treatment, Short-course).
Malaria is caused by Plasmodium protozoa (P. vivax, P. falciparum - malignant malaria), transmitted by female Anopheles mosquitoes.
Dengue and Chikungunya are transmitted by daytime biting female Aedes aegypti mosquitoes.

coreConcepts.title: 2. Major National Health Programmes in India
coreConcepts.content:
India operates targeted national programmes to curb disease burden:
1. NTEP (National TB Elimination Programme): Rebranded from RNTCP; aims to eliminate TB in India through Nikshay digital tracking, free molecular testing (CBNAAT/TrueNat), and nutritional support (Nikshay Poshan Yojana ₹500/month).
2. NVBDCP (National Vector Borne Disease Control Programme): Integrates control of 6 vector-borne diseases: Malaria, Filaria, Kala-azar, Japanese Encephalitis, Dengue, and Chikungunya.
3. Universal Immunization Programme (UIP) & Mission Indradhanush: Provides free vaccines against 12 vaccine-preventable diseases (TB, Diphtheria, Pertussis, Tetanus, Polio, Measles, Rubella, Hepatitis B, Meningitis/Pneumonia due to Hib, Rotavirus, Pneumococcal Conjugate Vaccine, Japanese Encephalitis).
4. Ayushman Bharat (Pradhan Mantri Jan Arogya Yojana - PM-JAY): World's largest government-funded healthcare scheme providing health cover of ₹5 lakh per family per year for secondary and tertiary care hospitalization.
ncertPointers: Mission Indradhanush was launched in December 2014 to ensure full immunization coverage for children and pregnant women.
Health and Wellness Centres (HWCs) under Ayushman Bharat deliver Comprehensive Primary Health Care (CPHC).

coreConcepts.title: 3. Hygiene and Community Health Infrastructure
coreConcepts.content:
Health is defined by WHO as 'a state of complete physical, mental, and social well-being and not merely the absence of disease or infirmity.'
Personal Hygiene: Regular bathing, oral hygiene, handwashing with soap (removes 99% of transient pathogenic microbes, prevents fecal-oral route transmission).
Community Health: Collective organized efforts of society to protect and improve the health of people. Key components: Safe municipal water supply (coagulation, sedimentation, filtration, chlorination), solid waste management (segregation at source: biodegradable vs non-biodegradable, composting, incineration, sanitary landfilling), and safe sewage disposal (primary mechanical settling, secondary biological oxidation).
ncertPointers: Chlorination of drinking water destroys pathogenic vegetative bacteria; recommended free residual chlorine is 0.5 mg/L after 30 minutes contact.
Primary Health Centres (PHCs) cover 30,000 population in plains and 20,000 in hilly/tribal areas.

keyFormulasAndTables.formula: Malaria -> Anopheles; Dengue/Chikungunya -> Aedes; Filaria -> Culex
keyFormulasAndTables.notes: Anopheles breeds in clean stagnant water; Aedes breeds in clean artificial containers (coolers, tyres).

keyFormulasAndTables.notes: Completely cashless and paperless access at empaneled hospitals.

workedExamples.question: Under the Ayushman Bharat - Pradhan Mantri Jan Arogya Yojana (PM-JAY), what is the maximum annual financial health cover provided per eligible family for secondary and tertiary care hospitalization?
solutionSteps: Step 1: Ayushman Bharat PM-JAY was launched in September 2018 as the world's largest health assurance scheme.
Step 2: The scheme provides a defined benefit cover of ₹5,00,000 per family per year on a family floater basis.
Step 3: This cover is fully cashless and portable across all empaneled public and private hospitals across India.
workedExamples.cuetTip: CUET regularly asks the exact financial cover limit (₹5 lakh) and the year of launch (2018) for PM-JAY.

workedExamples.question: Which of the following diseases is caused by a protozoan parasite and transmitted to humans specifically by the bite of an infected female Anopheles mosquito?
solutionSteps: Step 1: Malaria is caused by the protozoan Plasmodium (vivax, falciparum, malariae, ovale).
Step 2: The vector for malaria is the female Anopheles mosquito.
Step 3: Dengue and Chikungunya are viral infections transmitted by Aedes aegypti.
Step 4: Kala-azar is caused by Leishmania donovani and transmitted by the Sandfly (Phlebotomus).
workedExamples.cuetTip: Keep the vectors straight: Malaria = Female Anopheles; Dengue/Chikungunya/Yellow Fever = Aedes; Kala-azar = Sandfly; Filaria = Culex.

howCuetAsksThis.typicalStem: Match the Disease with its transmitting Vector (Malaria, Dengue, Kala-azar, Sleeping Sickness).
howCuetAsksThis.strategy: Pair Malaria with Anopheles, Dengue with Aedes, Kala-azar with Sandfly, Sleeping Sickness with Tsetse fly.

howCuetAsksThis.typicalStem:
Assertion (A): Non-communicable diseases like hypertension and Type 2 diabetes cannot be prevented by traditional vaccination.
Reason (R): NCDs are not caused by infectious pathogens; they stem from chronic physiological and behavioral lifestyle factors.
howCuetAsksThis.strategy: Both statements are factually sound and R correctly explains A.

commonTraps.misconception: Believing female Aedes mosquitoes bite exclusively at night.
commonTraps.whyWrong: Aedes aegypti (the dengue vector) is predominantly a daytime biter (peak biting during early morning and late afternoon before dusk).
commonTraps.correctUnderstanding: Anopheles bites mainly at night; Aedes bites primarily during daytime.
commonTraps.trapOptionExample: Option stating Dengue transmission occurs during midnight sleep.

commonTraps.misconception: Confusing DOTS strategy with diabetes therapy.
commonTraps.whyWrong: DOTS stands for Directly Observed Treatment, Short-course and is the WHO/NTEP global strategy for Tuberculosis.
commonTraps.correctUnderstanding: DOTS is exclusively for Tuberculosis bacteriological eradication.

practiceQuestions.question: Which of the following organisms causes Tuberculosis, and what is the primary organ it infects?
practiceQuestions.explanation: Tuberculosis is caused by the bacterium Mycobacterium tuberculosis and most commonly affects the lungs (pulmonary tuberculosis).

practiceQuestions.question: Which mosquito vector is responsible for transmitting the viruses causing Dengue fever and Chikungunya?
practiceQuestions.explanation: Female Aedes aegypti mosquitoes transmit both Dengue and Chikungunya viruses, breeding predominantly in artificial clean water containers.

practiceQuestions.question: According to standard clinical guidelines, what blood pressure reading indicates Stage 1 Hypertension?
practiceQuestions.explanation: Normal blood pressure is approximately 120/80 mmHg. Hypertension is clinically diagnosed when systolic blood pressure is ≥140 mmHg and/or diastolic pressure is ≥90 mmHg.

practiceQuestions.question: What is the primary objective of the government scheme 'Mission Indradhanush' in India?

options.text: Providing tap water connections to every rural household
Achieving full immunization coverage for all children and pregnant women
Constructing community toilets in tribal regions
Providing free school uniforms to girl students

practiceQuestions.explanation: Mission Indradhanush was launched by the Ministry of Health and Family Welfare to rapidly boost immunization coverage to over 90% for unvaccinated and partially vaccinated children and pregnant women.

practiceQuestions.question: What does the abbreviation 'DOTS' stand for in the context of the National Tuberculosis Elimination Programme?

options.text: Direct Observation of Treatment and Sanitation
Daily Oral Therapy for Sputum-positive cases

practiceQuestions.explanation: DOTS stands for Directly Observed Treatment, Short-course, the recognized internationally recommended strategy for TB control.

practiceQuestions.question: Which of the following biological control methods is officially deployed to curb mosquito larvae in freshwater ponds and stagnant pools?

options.text: Covering the pond with plastic sheets

practiceQuestions.explanation: Gambusia affinis (mosquitofish) is a larvivorous fish species widely introduced into freshwater bodies as an eco-friendly biological control agent that feeds voraciously on mosquito larvae.

practiceQuestions.question: What is the recommended standard population norm for setting up a Primary Health Centre (PHC) in plain areas of India?
practiceQuestions.explanation: In India, a Primary Health Centre (PHC) covers a population of 30,000 in plain areas and 20,000 in hilly, tribal, and difficult-to-reach areas.

practiceQuestions.question:
Assertion (A): Diseases such as Atherosclerosis and Type 2 Diabetes are classified as lifestyle disorders.
Reason (R): Their primary etiological drivers include physical inactivity, high saturated fat diets, and chronic psychological stress rather than microbial contagion.

options.text: Both (A) and (R) are true, and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
Both (A) and (R) are true, but (R) is NOT the correct explanation of (A).

practiceQuestions.explanation: Both (A) and (R) are true. Lifestyle disorders are non-communicable conditions arising directly from behavioral and daily life factors.

practiceQuestions.question:
Assertion (A): Drinking water treated with chlorine contains zero chemical residues after 30 minutes.
Reason (R): A free residual chlorine level of 0.5 mg/L is intentionally maintained to protect water against post-treatment secondary microbial contamination.

options.text: Both (A) and (R) are true, and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
Both (A) and (R) are true, but (R) is NOT the correct explanation of (A).

practiceQuestions.explanation: Assertion (A) is false because drinking water is explicitly kept with a small residual chlorine concentration (0.5 mg/L) to prevent recontamination in the distribution pipeline. Reason (R) is true.

practiceQuestions.question:
Match the Disease in List I with the Transmitting Vector / Mode in List II:
List I:
(P) Malaria
(Q) Dengue
(R) Typhoid
(S) Filariasis

List II:
(1) Contaminated water and food
(2) Female Anopheles mosquito
(3) Culex mosquito
(4) Aedes aegypti mosquito
practiceQuestions.explanation: Malaria = Female Anopheles (P-2); Dengue = Aedes (Q-4); Typhoid = Contaminated food/water (R-1); Filariasis = Culex mosquito (S-3). Matches A.
